gaps.text: In-line measurement of Broth optical density / turbidity with in-line optical density / turbidity sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: Raman and fluorescence spectra synchronised to a common time step and merged into one augmented matrix, with block scaling so neither method dominates. Both probes must sample the same broth volume, ideally via a combined or co-located probe head. Each method keeps its own calibration, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out batches or it is dropped.)
Whether glucose or viable biomass has ever been measured in-line by fluorescence with or without an added indicator; the supplied material does not cover this.
Measuring Viable biomass (viable cell concentration): It is the second target, and spectroscopy can only correlate with it, so an independent reference is needed.

items.finding: Turbidity-based measurements do not distinguish viable from non-viable biomass, which may affect performance in long fermentations.
items.how_it_applies: When using optical density or turbidity sensors for viable biomass estimation, watch for potential divergence in extended processes and consider complementary methods if viability distinction is required.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This limitation was noted in the context of yeast fermentations and may vary depending on the specific microbial species, cell lysis rates, and fermentation duration.

citation.quote: Finally, turbidity-based measurements do not distinguish viable from non-viable biomass, which may affect performance in long fermentations; integration with complementary methods such as capacitance-based sensors may be required (Kiviharju et al. 2008).

dropped.finding: Online optical probes operating at 860 nm provide continuous, non-invasive monitoring, but their signals become increasingly nonlinear due to multiple light scattering.
dropped.how_it_applies: Testing an in-line turbidity or optical density sensor can provide continuous signals for biomass assessment, though mathematical transformation may be needed to handle nonlinearity from scattering.
dropped.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited study used a specific 3 L bioreactor configuration and yeast species, so scale-up effects, mixing heterogeneities, and different cell morphologies may introduce bias and require recalibration.
